summary: The article provides a generally accurate and well-sourced overview of InvITs, their structure, benefits, and recent regulatory changes, with most claims verified by authoritative sources.

claims.claim: Just this week, on September 28, 2026, SEBI approved allowing Depository Receipts (DRs) against InvIT units, a move aimed at attracting more foreign capital into these vehicles.
claims.note: SEBI approved the proposal to allow DRs against REIT and InvIT units on September 28, 2026, to attract foreign capital.

claims.claim: There's also recent news from September 29, 2026, about IRB InvIT Fund completing a significant fund-raise of ₹2,351 crore through institutional placement and preferential allotment to acquire more highway assets.
claims.note: IRB InvIT Fund completed a fund-raise of ₹2,351 crore through institutional placement and preferential allotment, with the QIP allotment approved on September 29, 2026.

claims.claim: Furthermore, the National Highways Infra Trust (NHIT), sponsored by NHAI, recently engaged consultants for the operations and maintenance of its national highway assets, showing continued professional management of these trusts, with a decision taken on July 13, 2026.
claims.note: NHIT's Board approved engaging General Management Consultants for O&M on July 13, 2026.

claims.claim: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) also issued amendment directions on September 22, 2026, to clarify valuation norms for InvIT units held by financial institutions, ensuring uniform practices.
claims.note: RBI issued Amendment Directions, 2026, on September 22, 2026, to revise valuation norms for InvIT and REIT units held by financial institutions.

claims.claim: Experts predict that the combined assets under management (AUM) of InvITs and REITs could double to around ₹20 trillion by 2030-31, driven by continued asset monetisation and regulatory reforms.
claims.note: ICRA projects the combined AUM of InvITs and REITs to double to nearly ₹20 trillion by 2030-31 from ₹10 trillion in 2025-26.

claims.claim: A significant portion (at least 90% of the net distributable cash flow) of this income is regularly distributed to the unitholders (investors) as dividends or interest.
claims.note: SEBI regulations mandate InvITs to distribute at least 90% of their net distributable cash flows to unitholders.

claims.claim: India's Finance Bill 2026 introduced changes to simplify investor taxation for InvITs, effective from April 1, 2026.
claims.note: While taxation of InvITs is complex and changes occur, specific details of a 'Finance Bill 2026' simplifying investor taxation effective April 1, 2026, could not be definitively verified on incometax.gov.in or other regulatory sites with the provided search capabilities. General information about InvIT taxation is available, but not this specific bill and effective date.

claims.claim: Recent SEBI amendments in September 2025 also reduced the minimum investment threshold for InvITs from ₹1 crore to ₹25 lakhs for any investor.
claims.note: SEBI's Third Amendment to InvIT Regulations, 2014, notified on September 1, 2025, reduced the minimum investment threshold for privately placed InvITs from ₹1 crore to ₹25 lakhs.

article_title: Your Roads and Power Lines Just Got a New Way to Fund Themselves: Understanding InvITs
